author: historian-agent:gemini-flash-outline
title: Non-avian dinosaurs
summary: Non-avian dinosaurs were the dominant terrestrial vertebrates of the Mesozoic Era, originating in the Late Triassic around 232 million years ago and diversifying into hundreds of herbivorous and carnivorous species worldwide. Their extinction 66 million years ago at the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary, triggered by the Chicxulub asteroid impact, ended their roughly 166-million-year reign and opened ecological space for the adaptive radiation of mammals and modern birds.

uncertainty.note: Origin is dated to the early Late Triassic (Carnian stage, c. 237–228 Ma, commonly placed around 232 Ma); extinction is constrained to the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary at approximately 66.0 Ma.

as_recorded.value: extinction of non-avian dinosaurs at the end of the Cretaceous period (approximately 66 Ma)

when.display: c. 232–66 million years ago (Late Triassic to Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary)

where.modern_name: Hell Creek Recreation Area, Garfield County, Montana, United States (reference site for the latest Cretaceous dinosaur communities; the clade was globally distributed)
where.historical_name: Laramidia, western North America, Late Cretaceous; clade distributed across all continents from Pangaea through the Cretaceous

importance.justification: Non-avian dinosaurs dominated terrestrial ecosystems for over 160 million years, and their sudden extinction cleared the way for the Cenozoic radiation of mammals.

related.because: The Chicxulub asteroid impact triggered global environmental collapse that wiped out all non-avian dinosaurs.
The extinction of non-avian dinosaurs vacated ecological niches that surviving mammal lineages diversified into.
